articles.title: Stone Tools and Butchered Bones Push Back the Story of Chile's First Hunters
articles.summary: Archaeologists in central Chile found 13,000-year-old gomphothere bones with cut marks and stone tools beside them. The site adds key evidence about when the first humans reached South America and how they hunted giant extinct animals.

articles.title: The Dreaming Brain Burns Energy Even as Its Fuel Supply Rises
articles.summary: Researchers in Japan watched mice sleep and found a strange pattern: during REM sleep, blood flow to the brain increases, but the energy molecule neurons use actually drops. That paradox may explain why vivid dreams leave us feeling drained.

articles.title: CERN Begins Swapping Out Magnets in the Large Hadron Collider
articles.summary: Crews at CERN have started removing 28 superconducting magnets from the Large Hadron Collider. The new magnets will be about 40% stronger, creating more particle collisions and giving scientists more data to study.
